question: Are whole-file hash differences explained by absolute paths, by locale-dependent link order, or by code generation?
method: Two extra prepare=1 experiment builds under LC_ALL=C at different directory names (rebuild-1c, rebuild-2c), against the default-locale rebuild-1. Section bytes via `otool -s SEG SECT FILE | tail -n +3 | cut -f2- | shasum -a 256` (addresses stripped).
findings: rebuild-1c and rebuild-2c (both LC_ALL=C, different paths) have identical __text and __data bytes but different file hashes: the file-hash difference comes from path-dependent metadata (install_name, debug map, UUID), not code.
rebuild-1 (en_US.UTF-8) has different __text bytes from rebuild-1c: link order changes the code layout.

GNU Make 3.81 (/usr/bin/make) sorts $(wildcard) by locale collation: under en_US.UTF-8 gr_LOBJS gives fmpq_mpoly.lo fmpq_poly.lo fmpq.lo; under LC_ALL=C fmpq.lo fmpq_mpoly.lo fmpq_poly.lo. The pinned ld -r lists are in C (byte) order, so the pinned build ran under a C-collating locale or a different make.
not_checked: The pinned binaries are not committed, so pinned section bytes could not be compared; libflint.25.0.dylib in this session was built under en_US.UTF-8 and not rebuilt under LC_ALL=C. The 1c/2c build directories are scratch and not committed.
